fields.description:
## Context / Problem

Most plan-review criteria have no eval fixture, so a rubric edit ships with no behavioral
oracle. The selector must decide which reviews are trustworthy evidence of a criterion's
behavior — the corpus records what the reviewer SAID, not what was true. Two
hazards make naive selection wrong. Reviewer noise: 551 byte-identical-material review pairs
flipped verdict 208 times, so one observation is not a label. Prompt vintage: rubrics were
rewritten inside the corpus window, so a finding from a retired rubric does not describe
today's criterion (`regver`, `manifest.py:139-185`, hashes routing and ids, not rubric bytes).
`corpus.py` reconstructs at-review plan text (`corpus.py:270-288`) over 6,482 committed rows.

## Approach

An offline selector writing a LABELED CANDIDATE MANIFEST — per criterion, each candidate with
its direction, tier, signals and rank, plus a zero-candidate row (with reason) for every
criterion that produced none. The manifest is JSONL: one JSON object per line, keys sorted,
rows in the rank order below — a byte-stable contract for the diff AC and the emitter. No YAML,
no model call.

**Candidate key and signal join.** A FIRE candidate is keyed `(criterion, norm_id)`
(`sidecar.py:656,663`); signals join on that key, which is load-bearing because they live on
different pair relationships: `finding_survival` over consecutive DIFFERING-material pairs,
reproduction consensus over EQUAL-`material_fingerprint` pairs. A key in one relationship gets
that signal alone.

**Vintage gate.** A review is eligible for criterion C only when `review_event_ts`
(`corpus.py:273`) postdates the last commit touching C's rubric file. With
`pid = criterion_prompt_id(C)` the path resolves by `get_prompt`'s override-wins ordering
(`prompts.py:187-198`): `.rebar/prompts/<pid>.md` if present, else `reviewers/` joined to
`prompts.get_prompt(pid).fallback_file` (`prompts.py:196`). History is read
by `git log` against the gate's configured base ref (`gate_source.default_ref`, `origin/main`
by default); when that ref is absent (shallow clone, differently-named remote) or git errs, C
fails closed to a zero-candidate `no-committed-prompt-history` row rather than crashing — the
same row a criterion with no committed rubric history (an uncommitted override, or a post-freeze
rubric) records. The gate keys on git history alone, never on C's name.

Both label signals are Pass-1 finder observations from the historical sidecar, not Pass-2
verifier output, so only the criterion's own rubric vintage gates them; no
`plan-review-verifier` sub-gate applies.

**Label signals**, offline and independent of the reviewer's own verdict:
- *Reproduction consensus* — a key that fired, or stayed absent, consistently across two or
  more equal-`material_fingerprint` reviews. The only signal valid no-fire.
- *Author response* — `finding_survival == "resolved_by_author"` (`labels.py:158-171`), the
  only per-finding label the labels module produces. Fire direction only.

**No-fire admission.** A no-fire candidate has no fired finding and therefore no `norm_id`, so
it is keyed `(C, norm_id=None)` and admitted ONLY under the parent epic's predicate: C is in
the `cohort` set of some finding on that plan (`sidecar.py:667-672`, proving C was ROUTED) AND
no finding cites C; a missing-`cohort` row is skipped, never read as empty. Reproduction
consensus then RAISES an admitted no-fire candidate to ADVISORY — it is the ranking signal, not
the admission gate; absence-consensus alone never admits what the parent's predicate forbids.

**Escaped defect is a PRIORITY signal, not a label.** `escaped_defect` (`labels.py:70-73`) is
a per-TICKET bool with no criterion attribution, so as a label it would misattribute a
must-fire candidate; it only raises a review's rank. Its absence never evidences correct
silence, so `clean_close` (`labels.py:43`) is not a no-fire source.

**Tiered bar.** The vintage gate is a precondition of BOTH tiers: a failing candidate is
excluded, not downgraded. Among those passing, a FIRE candidate is BLOCKING only when all three
hold: reproduction consensus, author-response corroboration, and `abs(decision_margin)`
(`sidecar.py:344-360`) at or above `MIN_MARGIN = 0.15`. `decision_margin` is `None` (never
0.0) when either side was unrecorded, and a `None` margin never qualifies. Margin and
author-response are per-finding and fire-direction only, so a NO-FIRE candidate reaches at most
ADVISORY on consensus alone. Any single signal proposes ADVISORY.

**Rank order.** BLOCKING before ADVISORY, then escaped-defect priority, then descending
`abs(decision_margin)` with `None` margins sorting last, then ascending `review_event_uuid` as
a deterministic tie-break; the emitter then takes a fixed number per side.

**Skip list.** A criterion with an open `unreliable-criterion: <id>` ticket is skipped,
recorded as a zero-candidate row with that reason.

## Scope

A new module under `src/rebar/llm/evals/` holding the selector, its predicates and the JSONL
manifest writer, over `plan_replay/corpus.py` and `labels.py`. It covers only criteria
`criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')` reports with no spec in
`.rebar/evals/` or `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/`.

## Non-goals

- Writing any `.eval.yaml` or admitting a candidate (the emitter and admission runner own
  those); any model call; per-finding true/false-positive labelling and human adjudication.

## Testing

Unit tests over the predicates on synthetic corpus rows, plus one integration test over the
real corpus with no model; all assertions deterministic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A review predating its criterion's resolved rubric commit is excluded, an
      otherwise-identical later one included; `pytest` asserts the manifest holds only the
      second row's id.
- [x] The gate git-logs `.rebar/prompts/<pid>.md` for a criterion with an override and the
      packaged `fallback_file` for one without; `pytest` over the path.
- [x] A criterion excluded for either reason — no committed rubric history (incl. an
      unresolvable base ref) or an open `unreliable-criterion: <id>` ticket — carries a
      zero-candidate row naming it; parameterized `pytest` over an uncommitted override, an
      absent base ref, and a stubbed listing.
- [x] A fire candidate failing the vintage gate yields no row, not an advisory one; `pytest`
      asserts its absence.
- [x] Removing each of reproduction consensus, author-response and margin in turn downgrades a
      fire candidate to `advisory`, all three present yields `blocking`, and a `None` margin
      never yields `blocking`; parameterized `pytest` over the recorded tier.
- [x] A no-fire candidate is admitted only when C is in some finding's `cohort` on the plan and
      no finding cites C (missing-cohort skipped), keyed `norm_id=None`, and never `blocking`;
      parameterized `pytest`: a routed-and-silent key is `advisory`, a missing-cohort key and a
      cited key are both absent.
- [x] A candidate whose only signal is `escaped_defect` appears in no direction; one carrying
      it outranks an equal-signal peer; `pytest` over the list and ranks.
- [x] A key present only in equal-fingerprint pairs records reproduction consensus and no
      author-response signal; `pytest` asserts the recorded signal set.
- [x] Given 6 candidates on one side with distinct margins plus one `None` margin, the recorded
      ranks follow the stated order with `None` last; `pytest` over the ranks.
- [x] Two consecutive real runs over the committed corpus emit a byte-identical JSONL manifest
      under the repository's network guard; `diff` of the two files exits 0 with the guard
      active.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; the real-corpus run writes a manifest row
per uncovered criterion; `.rebar/evals/` is untouched.

## Budget

**$0.** Selection is a pure function of the corpus and git metadata.
